## 3. Required adversarial scenarios not established

The following requested scenarios are explicitly not represented as passes: an infinite progression task bounded by a hard global ceiling; retries across repeated `resume`; compaction repeatedly failing to shrink context; deep escalation that returns to the original model; external calls under cancellation; process/host restart at each durable write point; memory/file-descriptor/disk measurement under many concurrent sessions; and a full CI mutation test that attempts to disable required verification. Existing tests cover selected subcases, but no complete end-to-end adversarial campaign was run.

## 4. Reproduction notes

From a clean checkout of the audited revision, install CLI dependencies with `npm ci --prefix cli`; use a throwaway `HOME` and XDG directories for tests; for Rust, set a worktree-local `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. `npm --prefix cli test` is the full CI CLI suite and may take 12–30 minutes; this audit did not run it. The no-ceiling behavior is reproducible from `DEFAULT_CONTINUATION` and loop guards cited in AT-06; an empirical reset test should use the repository’s `startGateway` fixture and should preserve its source/output transcript outside the main checkout.
# Nexus Code Engineering Assurance Gap Analysis

**Assessment baseline:** `origin/main` at `a0329e72ea796a306ea138ab2870d15920e4af61` (2026-11-18, merge PR #624).  
**Audit type:** repository-grounded assessment; no production source was changed.  
**Primary reference:** Gerard J. Holzmann, [The Power of Ten – Rules for Developing Safety Critical Code](https://spinroot.com/gerard/pdf/P10.pdf), 6 pages. The paper frames rules as small, mechanically checkable restrictions to strengthen analysis and boundedness; its examples target C, not agent systems.

## 1. Executive assessment

**Verdict: INSUFFICIENT.** Nexus has stronger-than-usual runtime outcome typing, independent-verification logic, durable state transitions, provider recovery, command deadlines, and negative tests. These controls meaningfully reduce false success and make interruption visible. They do not establish that all autonomous execution is bounded or that repository acceptance rules are independent of the change being accepted.

The most consequential confirmed gaps are:

1. Normal agent turns default to infinite total steps and infinite wall time. They stop for completion, cancellation, an error, or detected stagnation, so a sequence that keeps making measured progress has no enforced ceiling. The delegated `runSubagent` path also has no turn/time cap. This is documented and tested behavior, not an accidental missing option (`cli/src/types.ts:182-188`, `cli/src/core/run_turn.ts:220-275`, `cli/src/agent.ts:4440-4457`; `cli/test/compaction_continuity.test.ts:58-73` and `:75-95`).
2. A continuation budget is evaluated against a local per-invocation step counter. Durable `cumulativeSteps` is reported but explicitly “never a limit”; starting a resumed turn constructs a fresh local step counter. Thus explicit `maxTotalSteps` and `maxTurnMinutes` do not bound a task across operator or process resumes (`cli/src/core/run_turn.ts:137-145`, `:220-267`, `:1019-1041`; `cli/src/core/turn.ts:348-359`).
3. Execution records are not authoritative tamper-evident evidence. The flight recorder sanitizes and appends locally, but catches append failures and has no integrity chain or signature (`cli/src/flight.ts:77-108`). GitHub currently requires three status checks but zero approving reviews; an accepted change can alter its own workflow or verification configuration without a repository-enforced independent approval (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`; live ruleset 25340146 queried 2026-11-18).

These findings do not erase real strengths. `VERIFIED` is a structured result with runtime invariants, passing-verifier requirements, no pending unverified changes, and nonzero exit code on weaker outcomes (`cli/src/core/turn.ts:420-479`). The normal turn path distinguishes provider failure, interruption, blocked work, verifier failure, and unverified completion. Recovery replay has deadlines, iteration and ambiguous-replay bounds; shell RPC has explicit deadlines; operation transitions are durably saved and cap a single runner invocation at 10,000 scheduler transitions (`cli/src/core/provider_recovery.ts:150-177`, `:383-432`; `cli/src/tools.ts:515-539`; `cli/src/core/operation_runner.ts:160-270`).

The system therefore demonstrates several important local guarantees, but not the end-to-end guarantee in the audit prompt: bounded autonomous execution across delegated and resumed paths, under an independently protected acceptance authority, with attributable evidence that cannot silently disappear or be rewritten.

| Runtime / languages | Node.js CLI in TypeScript (strict TS config); Rust 2024 core, Rust 1.95 toolchain. Node requirement `>=22` in root and CLI package manifests. |

These instructions were followed where applicable; they are not treated as implementation evidence. This audit changed documentation only in its isolated worktree.

## 3. Architecture inventory

| Subsystem | Actual boundary and evidence examined | Assurance characterization |
|---|---|---|
| Agent orchestration | `cli/src/core/run_turn.ts`, `cli/src/agent.ts`, `cli/src/core/operation.ts`, `operation_runner.ts`, `operation_runner_execution.ts`; continuation, delegated agent and operation tests. | Typed turn outcomes and scheduler state exist. Standard turns may continue without a total limit; operations have a per-process transition cap. |
| Tool execution | `cli/src/core/dispatch_tool_call.ts`, `cli/src/core/spine.ts`, `cli/src/tools.ts`, `core/src/runner.rs`. | Capability/policy dispatch produces receipts; Rust owns child process groups and cancellation; ordinary host commands remain powerful unless sandboxed/approved. Tool timeouts are explicit and capped by configured maximum. |
| Session management | `cli/src/session.ts`, `sidecar.ts`, `core/client_lease.ts`. | Session schemas, private directories, restore validation and a process lease exist. An operator can resume; each resumed `runTurn` starts a new per-turn budget. |
| Persistence | `cli/src/core/durable_file.ts`, `state.ts`, `task_message_log.ts`, `operation_runner_persistence.ts`. | Atomic temp-file/rename writes, optional fsync, schema validation, guarded stores and task/operation locks exist. These establish crash consistency for specific records, not general authenticated integrity against same-user edits. |
| Compaction | `cli/src/agent.ts`, `core/run_turn.ts`, archived-history methods in `session.ts`. | Compaction is recorded and source history archived before committed summaries; capacity admission and several failure paths are explicit. A global memory/disk budget is not enforced. |
| Recovery | `cli/src/core/provider_recovery.ts`, `operation_runner.ts`, `operation_runner_persistence.ts`. | Provider waits are deadline/iteration bounded; unknown inference replay is capped. Durable operation waits can persist indefinitely pending operator action. |
| Model routing | `cli/src/client.ts`, `core/resources.ts`, `provider_capabilities.ts`. | Typed failure classification, endpoint/provider capabilities and resource eligibility support constrained rerouting. Fallback is bounded per request path, not a task-wide spend/time budget. |
| Verification | `cli/src/core/completion_oracle.ts`, `independent_check.ts`, `spine_handlers.ts`, `dispatch_tool_call.ts`, `tester.ts`. | Passing tests alone do not automatically mean `VERIFIED`; verifier definition, baseline, tests, deliverable scope and current candidate are considered. Some verifier definitions are unbindable, correctly reducing the result to regression evidence. |
| Acceptance | `cli/src/core/turn.ts`, `run_turn.ts`, `spine_handlers.ts`, `operation_runner_execution.ts`, `index.ts`. | Typed outcome/exit code and runtime invariant checks fail closed for configured verifier failure, incomplete requirements and interrupted/blocked turns. No verifier can yield `UNVERIFIED`, not `VERIFIED`. |
| Evidence | `cli/src/evidence.ts`, `flight.ts`, `sidecar.ts`, verification receipt paths. | Structured, redacted records and candidate hashes exist. Flight log is local, best-effort and lacks tamper evidence; a “recorded” event may be omitted silently. |
| Configuration | `cli/src/config.ts`, `types.ts`, CLI options, environment overrides, `security.ts`. | Operator configuration is extensive and mostly validated. It can set no total continuation limit; project-local configuration and agent-editable workspace files are not all governed by a top-level immutable policy. |
| User interface | `cli/src/repl.ts`, `sidecar.ts`, `tui.ts`, `core/bin/nexus_tui.rs`, `ui.ts`. | Surfaces expose blocked/interrupted/unverified states; Rust TUI tests include exhaustive approval rendering checks. A model’s final prose is not the structured success predicate. |

The CERI code under `cli/src/ceri/` was found, but a search of production `cli/src` imports found no shipped import of that subsystem. It is therefore not counted as an operational acceptance control in this assessment. The roadmap itself describes later CERI slices; this audit does not infer current shipped behavior from those plans.

## 4. Holzmann’s original rules: applicability and finding

The original rules are C-oriented. Their safety intent transfers; literal restrictions such as banning all heap allocation or pointer indirection do not transfer to TypeScript/Rust without losing their rationale. The measurable adaptations and individual evidence are in [`POWER_OF_TEN_CONTROL_MATRIX.md`](POWER_OF_TEN_CONTROL_MATRIX.md).

| Rule | Adaptation to Nexus | Highest demonstrated maturity | Finding |

* **Verification policy outside model control — incomplete.** Tool dispatch has a verification-file edit policy; `task_completed` invokes the completion oracle; CI checks are configured. However policy and workflow files are code in the candidate repository and GitHub currently requires zero approving reviews. Passing CI is therefore not independent from the candidate’s ability to change that CI. (M3 for local verifier guard; M2 for external governance.)
* **Long-running recovery — robust state safety, incomplete aggregate containment.** Atomic writes, schema-aware restore, interruption records, unknown outcomes, process cleanup and operation receipts exist. Side-effectful command timeouts can end as “result unknown”; they are not exactly-once. Per-turn/provider limits do not create a task-wide spend/time bound; an operation may wait indefinitely and its runner transition counter resets on resume. (M3–M4 on specific recovery paths, M2 aggregate.)

## 6. Adversarial validation summary

Tests executed or inspected are itemized with dispositions and commands in [`POWER_OF_TEN_ADVERSARIAL_TESTS.md`](POWER_OF_TEN_ADVERSARIAL_TESTS.md). Executed: the Rust suite (393 tests passed), npm dependency install (27 packages, audit reported zero vulnerabilities), TypeScript build, and Rust Clippy with warnings denied. The full CLI suite and live inference tests were not used as proof at the time of this report. No live gateway inference, host restart, real power-loss, or multi-process shared-workspace destructive trial was run.

Notably, the repository contains a fake-gateway test that intentionally runs a progressing objective past 300 steps with no forced termination (`cli/test/compaction_continuity.test.ts:75-95`). This is evidence of the chosen unlimited-progress behavior, not a proof of a runaway defect under every model. The external service/host can still be made to stop it, but model-internal progress is not a hard resource boundary.

## 7. Critical weaknesses and operational risk

Risk details for every finding are machine-readable in `POWER_OF_TEN_FINDINGS.json`.

| Finding | Severity / priority | Likelihood | Blast radius | Detection / recovery |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No default aggregate turn/delegation budget | High / P0 | Reachable by ordinary default configuration; a model that keeps producing distinct, state-changing work can continue. | Session, repository workspace, provider spend, external side effects (subject to tool permissions). | Step count and tokens are visible, but no cap necessarily trips; operator cancellation is recovery, already-issued external effects may be irreversible. |
| Budget resets across resume and operation-runner invocation | High / P0 | Reachable whenever an operator/service resumes a still-progressing objective. | One task across repeated process runs; potentially shared worktree and external providers. | Per-turn records show exhaustion, but cumulative task budget is not the guard. Stop or manual inspection required. |
| CI/review authority not independent | Critical / P0 | Reachable for changes that edit workflows, test commands or policy; active ruleset has 0 required approvals. | Repository integrity and acceptance of incorrect code. | A green required check may be self-modified. ## Executive verdict: **INSUFFICIENT**

At `origin/main` commit `a0329e72ea796a306ea138ab2870d15920e4af61`, Nexus has meaningful fail-closed verification and recovery controls, but it cannot demonstrate bounded autonomous execution across default runs and resumes. Live GitHub settings also require no approving review, leaving CI and verifier changes without an independently required reviewer. The audit used Holzmann’s [original paper](https://spinroot.com/gerard/pdf/P10.pdf) as its starting reference.

## Five highest-impact findings

1. **Critical · M2 · CI/review authority is not independent.** The live ruleset requires three checks but zero approvals, no code-owner review, and non-strict status checks. A candidate can change the checks that evaluate it. Evidence: ruleset 25340146, queried 2026-11-18; workflow source at the audited revision.
2. **High · M2 · Default execution has no total step or time ceiling.** Continuation defaults are infinite, and the delegated subagent loop has no total cap. Evidence: `cli/src/types.ts:182-188`, `cli/src/core/run_turn.ts:220-275`, `cli/src/agent.ts:4440-4457`.
3. **High · M2 · Budgets reset across resume.** Per-run counters restart; persisted cumulative steps are observational, not a task-wide limit. Evidence: `cli/src/core/run_turn.ts:137-145,220-267`, `cli/src/core/turn.ts:348-359`. A focused test passed for a configured 12-step limit across three in-process segments; resume-reset behavior remains untested dynamically.
4. **High · M2 · Global resource limits are not demonstrated.** Per-tool and context limits exist, but product-wide memory, disk, provider-spend, and concurrent-session admission caps were not established. This is a suspected operational gap, not a reproduced resource-exhaustion defect.
5. **Medium · M2 · Flight logs cannot guarantee complete, tamper-evident history.** Append failures are swallowed and records lack a verifiable chain or signature. Evidence: `cli/src/flight.ts:77-108`. This weakens forensic assurance; it does not itself bypass the structured completion predicate.

## Existing strengths

- `VERIFIED` is a structured outcome with runtime invariants, verifier requirements, candidate binding, and nonzero exit codes for weaker outcomes.
- Mutations invalidate verification evidence; recovery does not trust persisted verifier baselines as proof.
- Persistence uses atomic writes, with explicit interruption and unknown-outcome handling in relevant paths.
- Provider recovery has deadlines, iteration limits, and a bounded replay policy.
- Rust tests, TypeScript build, and local Clippy with warnings denied passed. The focused continuation-budget test also passed.

These controls are real, but their coverage varies by execution path; passing tests do not demonstrate overall autonomous-workflow sufficiency.

## Verification limitations

The full CLI suite ran for more than 45 minutes, showed multiple failures and environment-dependent skips, then was interrupted before its aggregate summary (exit 130). Treat that run as **inconclusive**, not green; individual streamed results cannot classify the full suite. The host lacked the dedicated capped evaluation workspace required for some cases. No live inference, host restart, power-loss, or multi-session resource-measurement experiment was performed.

## Recommended implementation sequence

1. **P0 — Protect acceptance authority:** require independent/code-owner approval for workflow, verifier, policy, and harness changes; harden required checks.
2. **P0 — Add durable aggregate budgets:** carry step, time, inference, tool, and delegation budgets through subagents and resumes; exhaustion must remain non-success.
3. **P1 — Close resource and evidence gaps:** measure concurrent-session behavior, add admission bounds through existing resource/lease seams, and make required evidence loss explicit and verifiable.
4. **P2 — Strengthen CI analysis:** add Clippy as a required gate after baseline review; add targeted diagnostics for critical complexity.

## Artifacts

Created in the isolated audit worktree:

- [Gap analysis](/home/mike/nexus-wt/power-of-ten-audit/docs/assurance/POWER_OF_TEN_GAP_ANALYSIS.md)
- [Control matrix](/home/mike/nexus-wt/power-of-ten-audit/docs/assurance/POWER_OF_TEN_CONTROL_MATRIX.md)
- [Adversarial test report](/home/mike/nexus-wt/power-of-ten-audit/docs/assurance/POWER_OF_TEN_ADVERSARIAL_TESTS.md)
- [Implementation plan](/home/mike/nexus-wt/power-of-ten-audit/docs/assurance/POWER_OF_TEN_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md)
- [Machine-readable findings](/home/mike/nexus-wt/power-of-ten-audit/docs/assurance/POWER_OF_TEN_FINDINGS.json)

The findings JSON parsed and passed the required-field check.

## Repository status

The audit worktree is detached at `a0329e72ea796a306ea138ab2870d15920e4af61` with only the five new, uncommitted audit artifacts. The original checkout remains at `05e640076bec2cdf2047a60d8522a5f12fd4794e`; its pre-existing changes (`AGENTS.md`, `tasks/lessons.md`, `tasks/todo.md`, and untracked `docs/agents/`) were preserved.

At `origin/main` commit `a0329e72ea796a306ea138ab2870d15920e4af61`, Nexus has meaningful fail-closed verification and recovery controls, but it cannot demonstrate bounded autonomous execution across default runs and resumes. Live GitHub settings also require no approving review, leaving CI and verifier changes without an independently required reviewer. The audit used Holzmann’s [original paper](https://spinroot.com/gerard/pdf/P10.pdf) as its starting reference.

## Five highest-impact findings

1. **Critical · M2 · CI/review authority is not independent.** The live ruleset requires three checks but zero approvals, no code-owner review, and non-strict status checks. A candidate can change the checks that evaluate it. Evidence: ruleset 25340146, queried 2026-11-18; workflow source at the audited revision.
2. **High · M2 · Default execution has no total step or time ceiling.** Continuation defaults are infinite, and the delegated subagent loop has no total cap. Evidence: `cli/src/types.ts:182-188`, `cli/src/core/run_turn.ts:220-275`, `cli/src/agent.ts:4440-4457`.
3. **High · M2 · Budgets reset across resume.** Per-run counters restart; persisted cumulative steps are observational, not a task-wide limit. Evidence: `cli/src/core/run_turn.ts:137-145,220-267`, `cli/src/core/turn.ts:348-359`. A focused test passed for a configured 12-step limit across three in-process segments; resume-reset behavior remains untested dynamically.
4. **High · M2 · Global resource limits are not demonstrated.** Per-tool and context limits exist, but product-wide memory, disk, provider-spend, and concurrent-session admission caps were not established. This is a suspected operational gap, not a reproduced resource-exhaustion defect.
5. **Medium · M2 · Flight logs cannot guarantee complete, tamper-evident history.** Append failures are swallowed and records lack a verifiable chain or signature. Evidence: `cli/src/flight.ts:77-108`. This weakens forensic assurance; it does not itself bypass the structured completion predicate.

## Existing strengths

- `VERIFIED` is a structured outcome with runtime invariants, verifier requirements, candidate binding, and nonzero exit codes for weaker outcomes.
- Mutations invalidate verification evidence; recovery does not trust persisted verifier baselines as proof.
- Persistence uses atomic writes, with explicit interruption and unknown-outcome handling in relevant paths.
- Provider recovery has deadlines, iteration limits, and a bounded replay policy.
- Rust tests, TypeScript build, and local Clippy with warnings denied passed. The focused continuation-budget test also passed.

These controls are real, but their coverage varies by execution path; passing tests do not demonstrate overall autonomous-workflow sufficiency.

## Verification limitations

The full CLI suite ran for more than 45 minutes, showed multiple failures and environment-dependent skips, then was interrupted before its aggregate summary (exit 130). Treat that run as **inconclusive**, not green; individual streamed results cannot classify the full suite. The host lacked the dedicated capped evaluation workspace required for some cases. No live inference, host restart, power-loss, or multi-session resource-measurement experiment was performed.

## Recommended implementation sequence

1. **P0 — Protect acceptance authority:** require independent/code-owner approval for workflow, verifier, policy, and harness changes; harden required checks.
2. **P0 — Add durable aggregate budgets:** carry step, time, inference, tool, and delegation budgets through subagents and resumes; exhaustion must remain non-success.
3. **P1 — Close resource and evidence gaps:** measure concurrent-session behavior, add admission bounds through existing resource/lease seams, and make required evidence loss explicit and verifiable.
4. **P2 — Strengthen CI analysis:** add Clippy as a required gate after baseline review; add targeted diagnostics for critical complexity.

## Artifacts

Created in the isolated audit worktree:

- [Gap analysis](/home/mike/nexus-wt/power-of-ten-audit/docs/assurance/POWER_OF_TEN_GAP_ANALYSIS.md)
- [Control matrix](/home/mike/nexus-wt/power-of-ten-audit/docs/assurance/POWER_OF_TEN_CONTROL_MATRIX.md)
- [Adversarial test report](/home/mike/nexus-wt/power-of-ten-audit/docs/assurance/POWER_OF_TEN_ADVERSARIAL_TESTS.md)
- [Implementation plan](/home/mike/nexus-wt/power-of-ten-audit/docs/assurance/POWER_OF_TEN_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md)
- [Machine-readable findings](/home/mike/nexus-wt/power-of-ten-audit/docs/assurance/POWER_OF_TEN_FINDINGS.json)

The findings JSON parsed and passed the required-field check.

## Repository status

The audit worktree is detached at `a0329e72ea796a306ea138ab2870d15920e4af61` with only the five new, uncommitted audit artifacts. The original checkout remains at `05e640076bec2cdf2047a60d8522a5f12fd4794e`; its pre-existing changes (`AGENTS.md`, `tasks/lessons.md`, `tasks/todo.md`, and untracked `docs/agents/`) were preserved.

# Executing Plans

## Overview

Load plan, review critically, execute all tasks, report when complete.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the executing-plans skill to implement this plan."

**Note:** Tell your human partner that Superpowers works much better with access to subagents. The quality of its work will be significantly higher if run on a platform with subagent support (such as Claude Code or Codex). If subagents are available, use superpowers:subagent-driven-development instead of this skill.

## The Process

### Step 1: Load and Review Plan
1. Read plan file
2. Review critically - identify any questions or concerns about the plan
3. If concerns: Raise them with your human partner before starting
4. If no concerns: Create TodoWrite and proceed

### Step 2: Execute Tasks

For each task:
1. Mark as in_progress
2. Follow each step exactly (plan has bite-sized steps)
3. Run verifications as specified
4. Mark as completed

### Step 3: Complete Development

After all tasks complete and verified:
- Announce: "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch
- Follow that skill to verify tests, present options, execute choice

## When to Stop and Ask for Help

**STOP executing immediately when:**
- Hit a blocker (missing dependency, test fails, instruction unclear)
- Plan has critical gaps preventing starting
- You don't understand an instruction
- Verification fails repeatedly

**Ask for clarification rather than guessing.**

## When to Revisit Earlier Steps

**Return to Review (Step 1) when:**
- Partner updates the plan based on your feedback
- Fundamental approach needs rethinking

**Don't force through blockers** - stop and ask.

## Remember
- Review plan critically first
- Follow plan steps exactly
- Don't skip verifications
- Reference skills when plan says to
- Stop when blocked, don't guess
- Never start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - Ensures isolated workspace (creates one or verifies existing)
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

# Power of Ten Remediation Implementation Specification

**Planning baseline:** `origin/main` `a0329e72ea796a306ea138ab2870d15920e4af61`. This is an implementation handoff, not authorization to change production code. No dates are assigned.

## Design constraints

Reuse `ContinuationBudget`, `ExecutionTracker`, `ProviderRecoveryController`, `ResourceRegistry`, `TurnResult`, completion-oracle receipts, `DurableStateManager`, `OperationStore`, `FlightRecorder`, and existing GitHub rulesets. Do not add a parallel orchestrator, verifier, or evidence store. Every work package must preserve non-success outcomes for interruption, unknown side effects, failed verification, and missing mandatory evidence.

## WP-P10-01 — Protect the independent acceptance authority

**Priority:** P0 · **Complexity:** S/M · **Dependencies:** none.

**Gap/evidence:** A candidate can modify `.github/workflows/ci.yml` or verifier/test harness definitions while the live branch ruleset requires zero approvals. The active ruleset requires checks but does not bind their implementation to an independently protected version. Evidence: GitHub ruleset 25340146 (read 2026-11-18); `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `cli/src/core/spine_handlers.ts:75-160`.

**Affected surfaces:** repository ruleset, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, workflow/test/verifier paths, PR template and documented merge policy.

**Design / reuse:** Use GitHub’s existing ruleset and CODEOWNERS; do not build an in-repo policy service. Require at least one independent approval, require code-owner review for workflow, verifier, security policy, and CI harness changes, dismiss approvals after relevant pushes, require latest commit approval, and enable strict status checks. If supported by owner policy, run required checks from a protected reusable workflow pinned to a protected ref.

**Implementation steps:**

1. Enumerate the paths that define acceptance (`.github/workflows/**`, test runner scripts, verifier discovery/oracle code, security gate scripts, lockfiles/build config).
2. Add CODEOWNERS for those paths; add tests that assert the path list matches governance documentation.
3. Update ruleset to require review/code-owner approval and strict check freshness. Keep bypass actors empty or explicitly owner-controlled.
4. Add a canary PR/harness mutation that removes a required check or makes it unconditional and demonstrate merge is blocked by independent policy.
5. Document emergency bypass ownership and audit record.

**Required tests / acceptance:** API readback confirms required approvals >=1, code-owner approval, strict status checks, no unapproved bypass actor. Seeded workflow change without approval cannot merge. A normal workflow change with independent approval and green required checks can merge. Exact SHA and ruleset JSON archived.

**Migration / rollback:** Existing open PRs may require new approvals and reruns. Rollback is ruleset restoration only by repository owner; retain the last known ruleset export. Residual risk: repository administrators can alter rulesets outside source control.

## WP-P10-02 — Durable task-level execution budgets

**Priority:** P0 · **Complexity:** L · **Dependencies:** WP-P10-01 recommended first; can be implemented independently.

**Gap/evidence:** `DEFAULT_CONTINUATION` sets total steps and minutes to Infinity (`cli/src/types.ts:182-188`); `runTurnImpl` checks a local `currentStep` (`run_turn.ts:137-145,220-267`); `runSubagent` uses an unbounded `for (;;)` (`agent.ts:4440-4457`); resumed invocation recreates local counters while cumulative steps are observational only (`turn.ts:348-359`).

**Affected surfaces:** `types.ts`, `config.ts`, `run_turn.ts`, subagent execution in `agent.ts`, provider recovery, tool deadlines, durable objective/task state, operation runner and CLI/UI reporting.

**Design / reuse:** Extend `ContinuationBudget` and existing durable objective/operation records with a task budget id, maximum total steps/tool invocations/inference submissions/elapsed time/tokens, per-tool deadline and delegation depth. Persist consumed counters before/after side effects with `withDurableSync`. Child agents inherit the parent’s remaining budget; provider retry consumes the same inference allowance. A resumed task cannot regain budget. Require explicit operator-authorized budget renewal after exhaustion.

**Implementation steps:**

1. Define additive schema fields with migration defaults that do not silently claim prior counters are zero; old tasks resume in a conservative bounded mode or require explicit operator choice.
2. Add a shared budget tracker passed through direct turns, subagents, work units, provider recovery and tool dispatch.
3. Enforce before dispatch and before any retry; classify exhaustion as `BLOCKED`/`LIMIT_REACHED`, never `VERIFIED` or successful operation completion.
4. Add ceilings for response streaming and whole-turn wall time, including a finite total timeout for local inference streams; idle timeout remains separate.
5. Report dimension, configured limit, consumed amount and resume behavior in CLI/TUI result.

**Required tests / acceptance:** Model emits distinct writes indefinitely: run stops at exact step/tool/token/time budget with nonzero/non-success result. Nested subagent shares remaining budget. Repeated provider failures consume retry allowance. Exhaustion followed by process restart and resume does not reset counters. Resume near limit permits only remaining budget. A hung local tool and slow-drip stream stop by configured deadline. Budget persistence write failure prevents new side-effectful dispatch.

**Migration / rollback:** New config defaults may shorten formerly unlimited runs; provide an explicit operator override with a hard documented maximum, not Infinity. Keep old records readable. Rollback must not turn persisted exhausted state into zero; older binaries should refuse unsupported budget schema versions. Residual risk: already-running external calls may finish after cancellation or have unknown outcomes.

## WP-P10-03 — Acceptance evidence integrity and export

**Priority:** P1 · **Complexity:** M · **Dependencies:** WP-P10-01 for independent policy identity.

**Gap/evidence:** Flight events are append-only by convention, but append failures are ignored (`cli/src/flight.ts:77-108`); no chain/signature verification exists. `TurnResult` has `candidateId` and output SHA but not complete environment/policy identity (`cli/src/core/turn.ts:191-219`).

**Affected surfaces:** `flight.ts`, `evidence.ts`, completion oracle, durable state and audit commands.

**Design / reuse:** Add an evidence manifest to existing receipt/event structures. Chain each event over prior digest; include candidate tree/commit identity, verifier definition/config digest, command, tool/runtime versions, exit code, timestamp, actor/model/provider identity and policy version. Use an operator-supplied signing key only if explicitly configured; unsigned bundles must say “integrity checked, not signed.” Required acceptance evidence write failure must produce a visible non-success result; optional telemetry remains best effort and explicitly marked.

**Implementation steps:**

1. Define canonical event encoding and versioned manifest.
2. Chain existing records and add offline `verify` over an exported bundle; do not duplicate existing state storage.
3. Bind verification receipt to exact candidate and current policy/workflow identity.
4. Add redaction before hashing/export and retention controls.
5. Distinguish required acceptance receipts from optional flight telemetry.

**Required tests / acceptance:** Alter, delete, reorder, truncate or append an event; verification names the first broken sequence. Candidate mutation after verification invalidates receipt. Simulated disk-full/permission error prevents verified acceptance when the receipt is mandatory. Secret fixture remains absent from export. Exact manifest contains source revision, candidate digest, command, exit code and tool versions.

**Migration / rollback:** Legacy logs remain readable but classify `integrity=unverified_legacy`; never silently “upgrade” them to verified. Keep old export path read-only during migration. Residual risk: same-user can delete both evidence and local chain unless an external signed/immutable copy is retained.

## WP-P10-04 — Resource admission and cleanup envelope

**Priority:** P1 · **Complexity:** M/L · **Dependencies:** WP-P10-02.

**Gap/evidence:** Output/context and some sandbox process limits are bounded, but no product-wide active memory, session count, retained disk, provider token/spend or concurrent operation budget was demonstrated. Operation runner batches all ready assignments through `Promise.all` (`operation_runner.ts:276-299`).

**Affected surfaces:** `core/resources.ts`, operation scheduler/runner, client leases, tool runner, durable state/compaction and process cleanup.

**Design / reuse:** Add admission to existing `ResourceRegistry` and scheduler; cap concurrency by operator-configured memory/provider budget. Reuse Rust process registry, output ring buffer, sandbox pids limit, `client_lease`, per-operation lock and session archival. Do not create a parallel resource manager.

**Required tests / acceptance:** Third operation unit is not launched when configured concurrency/memory budget is exhausted. Cancellation releases admission and child processes. Repeated compaction/resume does not grow active context beyond configured bound; retained disk has deterministic quota/retention behavior. Fault injection at tool exit and process restart leaves no orphan child/process lease. Cross-session tests demonstrate no cross-workspace data access.

**Migration / rollback:** Start with advisory resource estimates, then enforce with operator-visible defaults; do not kill unrelated sessions. Rollback disables only the new admission layer while retaining process cleanup. Residual risk: OS estimates are approximate; host OOM remains an external failure mode without cgroups/container limits.

## WP-P10-05 — Compiler/static-analysis gate and hotspot metrics

**Priority:** P2 · **Complexity:** S/M · **Dependencies:** WP-P10-01 for protection of CI.

**Gap/evidence:** Strict TS build and CodeQL JS/TS are present; Clippy passed on this audit machine but `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does not run it. No Rust CodeQL or targeted complexity gate was found. `runTurnImpl` remains a critical large function.

**Affected surfaces:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `core/Cargo.toml`, TS configuration and targeted complexity documentation.

**Design / reuse:** Add `cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings` to the existing Linux CI job after a green pinned baseline. Keep Rust warnings scoped and justified rather than inventing a large analyzer bundle. Add a complexity report or thresholds only for critical high-change functions; avoid arbitrary whole-repository size caps.

**Required tests / acceptance:** CI runs Clippy on exact PR merge head; seeded warning fails. TypeScript strict build is verified on Node 22 and 24. A changed critical function crossing an agreed CC/nesting threshold requires review or decomposition. Workflow is protected by WP-P10-01.

**Migration / rollback:** If historical warnings appear on a new toolchain, baseline them narrowly with tracked expiry/owner; do not suppress globally. Rollback is removal of a specific analyzer job only with independent approval. Residual risk: static analysis cannot establish requirements correctness or provider behavior.

## Dependency-aware order

1. **WP-P10-01** governance/acceptance authority (P0).
2. **WP-P10-02** aggregate budgets across direct, delegated, retry and resume paths (P0).
3. **WP-P10-03** durable evidence and candidate/policy binding (P1; can start schema design in parallel after WP-P10-01).
4. **WP-P10-04** aggregate resource admission and cleanup (P1; budget counters feed this work).
5. **WP-P10-05** static-analysis/complexity gate (P2; protected by WP-P10-01).

Each package lands independently with its own negative tests. CI green on a PR is not proof the implementation is correct; hosted checks must be tied to the exact candidate and accepted under the protected review policy.

**Required tests / acceptance:** Alter, delete, reorder, truncate or append an event; verification names the first broken sequence. Candidate mutation after verification invalidates receipt. Simulated disk-full/permission error prevents verified acceptance when the receipt is mandatory. Secret fixture remains absent from export. Exact manifest contains source revision, candidate digest, command, exit code and tool versions.

**Migration / rollback:** Legacy logs remain readable but classify `integrity=unverified_legacy`; never silently “upgrade” them to verified. Keep old export path read-only during migration. Residual risk: same-user can delete both evidence and local chain unless an external signed/immutable copy is retained.

## WP-P10-04 — Resource admission and cleanup envelope

**Priority:** P1 · **Complexity:** M/L · **Dependencies:** WP-P10-02.

**Gap/evidence:** Output/context and some sandbox process limits are bounded, but no product-wide active memory, session count, retained disk, provider token/spend or concurrent operation budget was demonstrated. Operation runner batches all ready assignments through `Promise.all` (`operation_runner.ts:276-299`).

**Affected surfaces:** `core/resources.ts`, operation scheduler/runner, client leases, tool runner, durable state/compaction and process cleanup.

**Design / reuse:** Add admission to existing `ResourceRegistry` and scheduler; cap concurrency by operator-configured memory/provider budget. Reuse Rust process registry, output ring buffer, sandbox pids limit, `client_lease`, per-operation lock and session archival. Do not create a parallel resource manager.

**Required tests / acceptance:** Third operation unit is not launched when configured concurrency/memory budget is exhausted. Cancellation releases admission and child processes. Repeated compaction/resume does not grow active context beyond configured bound; retained disk has deterministic quota/retention behavior. Fault injection at tool exit and process restart leaves no orphan child/process lease. Cross-session tests demonstrate no cross-workspace data access.

**Migration / rollback:** Start with advisory resource estimates, then enforce with operator-visible defaults; do not kill unrelated sessions. Rollback disables only the new admission layer while retaining process cleanup. Residual risk: OS estimates are approximate; host OOM remains an external failure mode without cgroups/container limits.

## WP-P10-05 — Compiler/static-analysis gate and hotspot metrics

**Priority:** P2 · **Complexity:** S/M · **Dependencies:** WP-P10-01 for protection of CI.

**Gap/evidence:** Strict TS build and CodeQL JS/TS are present; Clippy passed on this audit machine but `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does not run it. No Rust CodeQL or targeted complexity gate was found. `runTurnImpl` remains a critical large function.

**Affected surfaces:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `core/Cargo.toml`, TS configuration and targeted complexity documentation.

**Design / reuse:** Add `cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings` to the existing Linux CI job after a green pinned baseline. Keep Rust warnings scoped and justified rather than inventing a large analyzer bundle. Add a complexity report or thresholds only for critical high-change functions; avoid arbitrary whole-repository size caps.

**Required tests / acceptance:** CI runs Clippy on exact PR merge head; seeded warning fails. TypeScript strict build is verified on Node 22 and 24. A changed critical function crossing an agreed CC/nesting threshold requires review or decomposition. Workflow is protected by WP-P10-01.

**Migration / rollback:** If historical warnings appear on a new toolchain, baseline them narrowly with tracked expiry/owner; do not suppress globally. Rollback is removal of a specific analyzer job only with independent approval. Residual risk: static analysis cannot establish requirements correctness or provider behavior.

## Dependency-aware order

1. **WP-P10-01** governance/acceptance authority (P0).
2. **WP-P10-02** aggregate budgets across direct, delegated, retry and resume paths (P0).
3. **WP-P10-03** durable evidence and candidate/policy binding (P1; can start schema design in parallel after WP-P10-01).
4. **WP-P10-04** aggregate resource admission and cleanup (P1; budget counters feed this work).
5. **WP-P10-05** static-analysis/complexity gate (P2; protected by WP-P10-01).

Each package lands independently with its own negative tests. CI green on a PR is not proof the implementation is correct; hosted checks must be tied to the exact candidate and accepted under the protected review policy.

---
name: using-git-worktrees
description: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback
---

# Using Git Worktrees

## Overview

Ensure work happens in an isolated workspace. Prefer your platform's native worktree tools. Fall back to manual git worktrees only when no native tool is available.

**Core principle:** Detect existing isolation first. Then use native tools. Then fall back to git. Never fight the harness.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace."

## Step 0: Detect Existing Isolation

**Before creating anything, check if you are already in an isolated workspace.**

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
```

**Submodule guard:** `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON` is also true inside git submodules. Before concluding "already in a worktree," verify you are not in a submodule:

```bash
# If this returns a path, you're in a submodule, not a worktree — treat as normal repo
git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree 2>/dev/null
```

**If `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON` (and not a submodule):** You are already in a linked worktree. Skip to Step 3 (Project Setup). Do NOT create another worktree.

Report with branch state:
- On a branch: "Already in isolated workspace at `<path>` on branch `<name>`."
- Detached HEAD: "Already in isolated workspace at `<path>` (detached HEAD, externally managed). Branch creation needed at finish time."

**If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (or in a submodule):** You are in a normal repo checkout.

Has the user already indicated their worktree preference in your instructions? If not, ask for consent before creating a worktree:

> "Would you like me to set up an isolated worktree? It protects your current branch from changes."

Honor any existing declared preference without asking. If the user declines consent, work in place and skip to Step 3.

## Step 1: Create Isolated Workspace

**You have two mechanisms. Try them in this order.**

### 1a. Native Worktree Tools (preferred)

The user has asked for an isolated workspace (Step 0 consent). Do you already have a way to create a worktree? It might be a tool with a name like `EnterWorktree`, `WorktreeCreate`, a `/worktree` command, or a `--worktree` flag. If you do, use it and skip to Step 3.

Native tools handle directory placement, branch creation, and cleanup automatically. Using `git worktree add` when you have a native tool creates phantom state your harness can't see or manage.

Only proceed to Step 1b if you have no native worktree tool available.

### 1b. Git Worktree Fallback

**Only use this if Step 1a does not apply** — you have no native worktree tool available. Create a worktree manually using git.

#### Directory Selection

Follow this priority order. Explicit user preference always beats observed filesystem state.

1. **Check your instructions for a declared worktree directory preference.** If the user has already specified one, use it without asking.

2. **Check for an existing project-local worktree directory:**
   ```bash
   ls -d .worktrees 2>/dev/null     # Preferred (hidden)
   ls -d worktrees 2>/dev/null      # Alternative
   ```
   If found, use it. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.

3. **Check for an existing global directory:**
   ```bash
   project=$(basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)")
   ls -d ~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/$project 2>/dev/null
   ```
   If found, use it (backward compatibility with legacy global path).

4. **If there is no other guidance available**, default to `.worktrees/` at the project root.

#### Safety Verification (project-local directories only)

**MUST verify directory is ignored before creating worktree:**

```bash
git check-ignore -q .worktrees 2>/dev/null || git check-ignore -q worktrees 2>/dev/null
```

**If NOT ignored:** Add to .gitignore, commit the change, then proceed.

**Why critical:** Prevents accidentally committing worktree contents to repository.

Global directories (`~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/`) need no verification.

#### Create the Worktree

```bash
project=$(basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)")

# Determine path based on chosen location
# For project-local: path="$LOCATION/$BRANCH_NAME"
# For global: path="~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/$project/$BRANCH_NAME"

git worktree add "$path" -b "$BRANCH_NAME"
cd "$path"
```

**Sandbox fallback:** If `git worktree add` fails with a permission error (sandbox denial), tell the user the sandbox blocked worktree creation and you're working in the current directory instead. Then run setup and baseline tests in place.

## Step 3: Project Setup

Auto-detect and run appropriate setup:

```bash
# Node.js
if [ -f package.json ]; then npm install; fi

# Rust
if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then cargo build; fi

# Python
if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then poetry install; fi

# Go
if [ -f go.mod ]; then go mod download; fi
```

## Step 4: Verify Clean Baseline

Run tests to ensure workspace starts clean:

```bash
# Use project-appropriate command
npm test / cargo test / pytest / go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:** Report failures, ask whether to proceed or investigate.

**If tests pass:** Report ready.

### Report

```
Worktree ready at <full-path>
Tests passing (<N> tests, 0 failures)
Ready to implement <feature-name>
```

## Quick Reference

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Already in linked worktree | Skip creation (Step 0) |
| In a submodule | Treat as normal repo (Step 0 guard) |
| Native worktree tool available | Use it (Step 1a) |
| No native tool | Git worktree fallback (Step 1b) |
| `.worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| `worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| Both exist | Use `.worktrees/` |
| Neither exists | Check instruction file, then default `.worktrees/` |
| Global path exists | Use it (backward compat) |
| Directory not ignored | Add to .gitignore + commit |
| Permission error on create | Sandbox fallback, work in place |
| Tests fail during baseline | Report failures + ask |
| No package.json/Cargo.toml | Skip dependency install |

## Common Mistakes

### Fighting the harness

- **Problem:** Using `git worktree add` when the platform already provides isolation
- **Fix:** Step 0 detects existing isolation. Step 1a defers to native tools.

### Skipping detection

- **Problem:** Creating a nested worktree inside an existing one
- **Fix:** Always run Step 0 before creating anything

### Skipping ignore verification

- **Problem:** Worktree contents get tracked, pollute git status
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

### Assuming directory location

- **Problem:** Creates inconsistency, violates project conventions
- **Fix:** Follow priority: existing > global legacy > instruction file > default

### Proceeding with failing tests

- **Problem:** Can't distinguish new bugs from pre-existing issues
- **Fix:** Report failures, get explicit permission to proceed

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Create a worktree when Step 0 detects existing isolation
- Use `git worktree add` when you have a native worktree tool (e.g., `EnterWorktree`). This is the #1 mistake — if you have it, use it.
- Skip Step 1a by jumping straight to Step 1b's git commands
- Create worktree without verifying it's ignored (project-local)
- Skip baseline test verification
- Proceed with failing tests without asking

**Always:**
- Run Step 0 detection first
- Prefer native tools over git fallback
- Follow directory priority: existing > global legacy > instruction file > default
- Verify directory is ignored for project-local
- Auto-detect and run project setup
- Verify clean test baseline
# Running multiple agents on this plan without collisions

These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Nexus itself, or a human) that implements any part of this package at the same time as another. The repository's root `AGENTS.md` points here. The rules come from incidents recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`:

- a concurrent agent overwrote newer evidence;
- full test suites were contaminated by edits made mid-run;
- `pkill -f` killed the agent's own shell;
- HEAD moved during a pause.

They also follow from audit finding PER-03: the test suite writes into the real `~/.nexus`.

## 1. Unit of work: one claimed PR slice per agent

- The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.
- An agent works on exactly one claimed slice at a time.
- An agent must not edit files outside its slice's boundary. The exceptions are the ledger rows and the shared files covered by §4. If the work needs a file outside the boundary, the agent stops and records a **boundary request** (§6). It does not edit the file.

## 2. Claiming a slice (atomic and machine-local)

Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.

```sh
CLAIMS="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims"
mkdir -p "$CLAIMS"
SLICE="PLAN-01_PR-1a"
if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
  printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
    "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
else
  echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
fi
```

- **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
- **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
- **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
- If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.

## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes

| Resource | Rule |
|---|---|
| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
| Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
| HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
| Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
| Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
| Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
| Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
| Full test suites | The PTY and provider tests are timing-sensitive. Take the claim `SUITE` before running a full suite (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). While anyone holds `SUITE`, nobody runs other suites or targeted test files on the same machine. Concurrent load caused a false failure on 2026-10-15: `cloud_providers` saw an extra provider request after a load-induced timeout. Release the claim when the run ends. |
| Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
| Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |

## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly

These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.

| File | Plans that touch it | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
| `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tools.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 06, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-02 PR-2b (signal plumbing) lands before PLAN-03 PR-3c (`safeFetch`)**. |
| `cli/src/sidecar.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/doctor.ts` | 01, 03, 05, 06, 08 | Claim required. Each plan adds **new check functions** in separate blocks. Only PLAN-06 PR-6d changes existing checks. |
| `cli/src/client.ts` | 03, 05, 08, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-03 PR-3a (env layering) lands before any PLAN-05 slice.** |
| `cli/src/repl.ts` | 01, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/config.ts`, `security.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `plugins.ts` | 01, 03 | Claim required. PLAN-01 PR-1e and PLAN-03 must not run at the same time on `sandbox.ts` or `security.ts`. |
| `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts` | 01, 02 | **PLAN-01 PR-1a (effect classes) lands first.** PLAN-02 PR-2c adds schema fields afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tester.ts` | 01, 11 | **PLAN-01 PR-1c lands before PLAN-11 PR-11b/11c.** |
| `cli/src/core/state.ts` | 04, 08 | **PLAN-08 PR-8a (HOME isolation) lands before everything.** |
| `core/src/runner.rs`, `core/src/main.rs` | 01, 02, 06 | Claim required. The protocol version number is owned by PLAN-02 PR-2a. PLAN-06 PR-6c only reads it. |
| `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/{live_state,live_view}.rs` | 01, 02 | Claim required |
| `package.json`, `cli/package.json`, `core/Cargo.toml`, lockfiles | 01, 06, 07, 08 | **Only one agent at a time.** Version fields are written only by `scripts/sync-version.mjs`. Dependency changes are separate commits that touch only the lockfile and manifest. |
| `harness.sh`, `install.sh`, `scripts/package-linux.sh`, `.github/workflows/*` | 05, 06, 07, 09, C1 | Claim required. Workflow edits are separate commits. |
| `cli/dist/**` | all, while tracked | Do not commit `cli/dist` from slices. PLAN-07 PR-7d untracks it (DEC-10). Until that merges, only the merging agent rebuilds and commits dist, in a final separate commit, after rebasing. |
| `docs/USER_MANUAL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md`, `quickstart.md` | 05, 09 and doc tasks in every plan | Edit only the sections your slice changes. Hold a short `FILE_` claim. |

### Ledger updates (`docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md`)

A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.

## 5. Commit and merge discipline

1. Before **every** commit, compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit you last made. Then run `git log <yours>..HEAD` on the branch. If anything foreign appears, stop and reconcile. Never commit generated artifacts (evidence, dist, lockfiles) over a branch that moved (lessons 2026-10-13).
2. Commits are scoped to the slice. Do not reformat or clean up files outside the boundary.
3. Merge order follows the precedence rules in §4 and the ROADMAP milestone order. Within a milestone, the slice with fewer hot-file claims merges first.
4. Rebase onto `origin/main` immediately before merging. Re-run the slice's targeted tests, plus `make test`, on a snapshot of the rebased commit. Merge only if both pass.
5. Pushing, tagging, publishing and changing GitHub state (issues, milestones, releases) are **owner-approved actions** (DECISIONS X-list). Agents prepare them and do not perform them.
6. Preserve unrelated user work: the untracked `nexus-continuity-validation/`, the stashes, and any dirty files you did not create. Never stash, reset, clean or check out over them.

## 6. Coordination records

| Record | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Claims | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/` | Who owns which slice or file right now |
| Claim log | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims.log` (append-only, one line per event) | Claim, release, broken claim, boundary request |
| Boundary requests and discovered requirements | The PR description, under the heading `Needs from other slices`. Mirrored as one line in the claim log. | So the owning slice's agent can pick it up. Never fixed silently out of scope. |
| Slice evidence | `docs/reviews/evidence/v1/<plan>-<slice>/` (new directory per slice) | No shared evidence files, so agents cannot overwrite each other's evidence |

## 7. Safe parallel lanes

The following groupings can run at the same time with no hot-file contention beyond §4 claims. They are listed by milestone.

| Phase | Parallel lanes |
|---|---|
| M0 | (a) PLAN-08 PR-8a, which must merge first. Then in parallel: (b) PLAN-06 PR-6a, (c) PLAN-09 PR-9a. |
| M1 | (a) PLAN-01 PR-1a → PR-1b → PR-1c (sequential, owns `capabilities.ts`, `agent.ts` dispatch). (b) PLAN-02 PR-2a (Rust only). (c) PLAN-03 PR-3a → PR-3b (config/egress). (d) PLAN-11 PR-11a (`parser.ts`) and PR-11b (`tester.ts`, after PR-1c). Lanes (b), (c) and (d) do not touch `capabilities.ts`. |
| M2 (alongside M1) | (a) PLAN-07 PR-7a/7b/7c (workflows, scripts). (b) PLAN-06 PR-6b after PLAN-01 PR-1b (shares `index.ts` flags). |
| M3 | (a) PLAN-04 (`agent.ts` turn, operation runner). (b) PLAN-05 (`client.ts`, provider modules). (c) PLAN-10 harness (`eval/`, no product files). (d) Held-out task authoring by the agent author, **outside the repository**: no access to Nexus source or the development set (DEC-05). |
| M4 (alongside M3) | PLAN-08 PR-8b..8e. Coordinate with PLAN-04 on `state.ts` through `FILE_` claims. |
| M5 | **Serial on `GATEWAY`.** The eval runner, the stripped-proxy runs and the independent reviewer's live task each take the `GATEWAY` claim. The terminal matrix (E3) and the install matrix (E2) can run in parallel with gateway runs. |

## 8. Independence constraints

- The held-out task author must not see Nexus source, the development tasks or tuning history. It runs in a separate session with only the task schema and external repositories. Its output is sealed by a sha256 manifest committed before RC1.
- The independent reviewer in ACCEPTANCE §8 must not be the agent or session that implemented the slices under review.
- An implementing agent never edits `eval/heldout-manifest.json`, scorer thresholds or ACCEPTANCE §6.4 after the freeze.

# Using Git Worktrees

## Overview

Ensure work happens in an isolated workspace. Prefer your platform's native worktree tools. Fall back to manual git worktrees only when no native tool is available.

**Core principle:** Detect existing isolation first. Then use native tools. Then fall back to git. Never fight the harness.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace."

## Step 0: Detect Existing Isolation

**Before creating anything, check if you are already in an isolated workspace.**

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
```

**Submodule guard:** `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON` is also true inside git submodules. Before concluding "already in a worktree," verify you are not in a submodule:

```bash
# If this returns a path, you're in a submodule, not a worktree — treat as normal repo
git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree 2>/dev/null
```

**If `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON` (and not a submodule):** You are already in a linked worktree. Skip to Step 3 (Project Setup). Do NOT create another worktree.

Report with branch state:
- On a branch: "Already in isolated workspace at `<path>` on branch `<name>`."
- Detached HEAD: "Already in isolated workspace at `<path>` (detached HEAD, externally managed). Branch creation needed at finish time."

**If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (or in a submodule):** You are in a normal repo checkout.

Has the user already indicated their worktree preference in your instructions? If not, ask for consent before creating a worktree:

> "Would you like me to set up an isolated worktree? It protects your current branch from changes."

Honor any existing declared preference without asking. If the user declines consent, work in place and skip to Step 3.

## Step 1: Create Isolated Workspace

**You have two mechanisms. Try them in this order.**

### 1a. Native Worktree Tools (preferred)

The user has asked for an isolated workspace (Step 0 consent). Do you already have a way to create a worktree? It might be a tool with a name like `EnterWorktree`, `WorktreeCreate`, a `/worktree` command, or a `--worktree` flag. If you do, use it and skip to Step 3.

Native tools handle directory placement, branch creation, and cleanup automatically. Using `git worktree add` when you have a native tool creates phantom state your harness can't see or manage.

Only proceed to Step 1b if you have no native worktree tool available.

### 1b. Git Worktree Fallback

**Only use this if Step 1a does not apply** — you have no native worktree tool available. Create a worktree manually using git.

#### Directory Selection

Follow this priority order. Explicit user preference always beats observed filesystem state.

1. **Check your instructions for a declared worktree directory preference.** If the user has already specified one, use it without asking.

2. **Check for an existing project-local worktree directory:**
   ```bash
   ls -d .worktrees 2>/dev/null     # Preferred (hidden)
   ls -d worktrees 2>/dev/null      # Alternative
   ```
   If found, use it. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.

3. **Check for an existing global directory:**
   ```bash
   project=$(basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)")
   ls -d ~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/$project 2>/dev/null
   ```
   If found, use it (backward compatibility with legacy global path).

4. **If there is no other guidance available**, default to `.worktrees/` at the project root.

#### Safety Verification (project-local directories only)

**MUST verify directory is ignored before creating worktree:**

```bash
git check-ignore -q .worktrees 2>/dev/null || git check-ignore -q worktrees 2>/dev/null
```

**If NOT ignored:** Add to .gitignore, commit the change, then proceed.

**Why critical:** Prevents accidentally committing worktree contents to repository.

Global directories (`~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/`) need no verification.

#### Create the Worktree

```bash
project=$(basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)")

# Determine path based on chosen location
# For project-local: path="$LOCATION/$BRANCH_NAME"
# For global: path="~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/$project/$BRANCH_NAME"

git worktree add "$path" -b "$BRANCH_NAME"
cd "$path"
```

**Sandbox fallback:** If `git worktree add` fails with a permission error (sandbox denial), tell the user the sandbox blocked worktree creation and you're working in the current directory instead. Then run setup and baseline tests in place.

## Step 3: Project Setup

Auto-detect and run appropriate setup:

```bash
# Node.js
if [ -f package.json ]; then npm install; fi

# Rust
if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then cargo build; fi

# Python
if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then poetry install; fi

# Go
if [ -f go.mod ]; then go mod download; fi
```

## Step 4: Verify Clean Baseline

Run tests to ensure workspace starts clean:

```bash
# Use project-appropriate command
npm test / cargo test / pytest / go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:** Report failures, ask whether to proceed or investigate.

**If tests pass:** Report ready.

### Report

```
Worktree ready at <full-path>
Tests passing (<N> tests, 0 failures)
Ready to implement <feature-name>
```

## Quick Reference

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Already in linked worktree | Skip creation (Step 0) |
| In a submodule | Treat as normal repo (Step 0 guard) |
| Native worktree tool available | Use it (Step 1a) |
| No native tool | Git worktree fallback (Step 1b) |
| `.worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| `worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| Both exist | Use `.worktrees/` |
| Neither exists | Check instruction file, then default `.worktrees/` |
| Global path exists | Use it (backward compat) |
| Directory not ignored | Add to .gitignore + commit |
| Permission error on create | Sandbox fallback, work in place |
| Tests fail during baseline | Report failures + ask |
| No package.json/Cargo.toml | Skip dependency install |

## Common Mistakes

### Fighting the harness

- **Problem:** Using `git worktree add` when the platform already provides isolation
- **Fix:** Step 0 detects existing isolation. Step 1a defers to native tools.

### Skipping detection

- **Problem:** Creating a nested worktree inside an existing one
- **Fix:** Always run Step 0 before creating anything

### Skipping ignore verification

- **Problem:** Worktree contents get tracked, pollute git status
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

### Assuming directory location

- **Problem:** Creates inconsistency, violates project conventions
- **Fix:** Follow priority: existing > global legacy > instruction file > default

### Proceeding with failing tests

- **Problem:** Can't distinguish new bugs from pre-existing issues
- **Fix:** Report failures, get explicit permission to proceed

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Create a worktree when Step 0 detects existing isolation
- Use `git worktree add` when you have a native worktree tool (e.g., `EnterWorktree`). This is the #1 mistake — if you have it, use it.
- Skip Step 1a by jumping straight to Step 1b's git commands
- Create worktree without verifying it's ignored (project-local)
- Skip baseline test verification
- Proceed with failing tests without asking

**Always:**
- Run Step 0 detection first
- Prefer native tools over git fallback
- Follow directory priority: existing > global legacy > instruction file > default
- Verify directory is ignored for project-local
- Auto-detect and run project setup
- Verify clean test baseline
# Running multiple agents on this plan without collisions

These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Nexus itself, or a human) that implements any part of this package at the same time as another. The repository's root `AGENTS.md` points here. The rules come from incidents recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`:

- a concurrent agent overwrote newer evidence;
- full test suites were contaminated by edits made mid-run;
- `pkill -f` killed the agent's own shell;
- HEAD moved during a pause.

They also follow from audit finding PER-03: the test suite writes into the real `~/.nexus`.

## 1. Unit of work: one claimed PR slice per agent

- The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.
- An agent works on exactly one claimed slice at a time.
- An agent must not edit files outside its slice's boundary. The exceptions are the ledger rows and the shared files covered by §4. If the work needs a file outside the boundary, the agent stops and records a **boundary request** (§6). It does not edit the file.

## 2. Claiming a slice (atomic and machine-local)

Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.

```sh
CLAIMS="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims"
mkdir -p "$CLAIMS"
SLICE="PLAN-01_PR-1a"
if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
  printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
    "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
else
  echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
fi
```

- **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
- **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
- **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
- If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.

## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes

| Resource | Rule |
|---|---|
| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
| Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
| HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
| Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
| Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
| Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
| Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
| Full test suites | The PTY and provider tests are timing-sensitive. Take the claim `SUITE` before running a full suite (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). While anyone holds `SUITE`, nobody runs other suites or targeted test files on the same machine. Concurrent load caused a false failure on 2026-10-15: `cloud_providers` saw an extra provider request after a load-induced timeout. Release the claim when the run ends. |
| Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
| Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |

## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly

These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.
